payload.rationale: I estimate a 55% chance that the Chargers win the September 20 game outright. The supplied report places the game at their home stadium, supporting a modest advantage as a general football assumption, not a measured matchup effect. Las Vegas has the stronger observed opening result: a 27–13 win versus the Chargers’ 14–26 loss. That shifts my assessment toward the Raiders, but one game against unspecified opponents is weak evidence of underlying strength. Brock Bowers being doubtful and Darien Porter being out hurt Las Vegas’s outlook, while the Chargers’ offensive-line and defensive absences and Ladd McConkey’s questionable status offset some of that benefit. I do not assume Aidan O’Connell’s designation establishes the availability of the Raiders’ starting quarterback. The estimate could be too high if the opening results reflect a genuine Raiders strength advantage or Chargers injuries materially impair their offense. It could be too low if those results were mostly opponent-driven noise and Bowers’s likely absence substantially weakens Las Vegas. This is an outright-win probability, not an expected settlement payout; a tie is not counted as a win.
limitations: Only one game of 2026 results is supplied for each team, without opponent adjustment.
No verified starting-quarterback information, complete roster assessment, final inactive list, or fitted strength model is available.
Home-field and injury effects are qualitative transfer assumptions, not estimated matchup-specific effects.
The evidence lists kickoff at 20:05 UTC, after the stated 16:00 UTC event deadline; this forecast concerns the eventual result of the contract-defined game.
Ties and cancellation-related settlements are distinct from an outright Chargers win; their probabilities have not been separately modeled.
